content.title: Where to watch Cardinals vs. Mets MLB game today on free streams, TV
content.text: New York Mets shortstop Bo Bichette (19) pumps his fist as the Mets win the opening-day baseball game against the Pittsburgh Pirates, Thursday, March 26, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Angelina Katsanis)APIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Dustin Hockensmith | dhockensmith@pennlive.comThe St. Louis Cardinals and New York Mets wrap a mid-week series with a Game 3 rubber match Wednesday afternoon in St. Louis. The game is scheduled to start at 1:15 p.m. ET (12:15 p.m. CT) with TV coverage on ESPN Unlimited and streaming on-demand.MLB on ESPN Unlimited: Major League Baseball, MLB Network and MLB.tv now reside in ESPN Unlimited’s interface. This game will stream on ESPN Unlimited, which is available as a standalone product ($29.99/month) and features all ESPN channels and ESPN+ access. ESPN Unlimited is also available through streaming services FuboTV (free trial) and DirecTV (free trial).Access to MLB.tv requires an additional fee, either annually for $134.99 (ESPN Unlimited subscribers) or $149.99 (non-subscribers) or monthly for $29.99. The monthly plan comes with one free month of ESPN Unlimited.How to watch Cardinals vs. Mets on TV and stream without cable:When: Wednesday, April 1 at 1:15 p.m. ET (12:15 p.m. CT)Where: Busch Stadium, St. Louis, Mo.TV channel: ESPN UnlimitedStreaming on: FuboTV (free trial) | DirecTV (free trial) | ESPN Unlimited ($29.99/mo.)Cardinals vs. Mets: The matchupThe Cardinals evened the score Tuesday night after the Mets opened with a 4-2 victory in Monday’s opener, holding the New York offense to three hits in a 3-0 shutout win. Catcher Ivan Herrera delivered a big blow early with a two-run double in the third, and third baseman Ramon Urias launched a 409-foot solo home run in the seventh to make a winner of starter Andre Pallante, who tossed five scoreless innings with three hits allowed, three strikeouts and three walks. The Mets are solid road favorites (-168) in the early betting line for Wednesday’s series finale, as they give the ball to No. 1 starter Freddy Peralta (1-0, 7.20 ERA) for his second start of the season. The Cardinals get back to the top of their rotation, too, and left-hander Matthew Liberatore, who allowed one run on five hits in seven innings in the Cards’ Opening Day win over the Tampa Bay Rays (9-7). Cardinals vs. Mets: Know your live streamsFuboTV (free trial): FuboTV offers the most extensive package of live sports with rates competitive with DirecTV. The FuboTV Pro ($48.99 first month), Elite ($53.99) and Deluxe ($73.99) all come with first-month discounts. Fubo streaming plans include access to ESPN Unlimited.DirecTV (free trial): DirecTV offers a 5-day free trial and a total of $30 off over the first three full months for the Choice Package, which includes 125-plus channels and access to ESPN Unlimited, a $29.99 standalone value featuring all ESPN channels and ESPN+.ESPN Unlimited ($29.99 bundle): ESPN has a new, standalone package that includes ABC broadcasts, all of ESPN’s sports channels, and access to ESPN+. For a limited time, ESPN can be bundled with Disney Plus and Hulu for $29.99 per month. This package is included free in select FuboTV and DirecTV plans, along with other TV providers.
